title: IICT and Wacom India Sign Strategic MoU at 57th IFFI to Strengthen India-Japan Creative Collaboration
subtitle: Initiative to support AVGC-XR talent through scholarships, professional tools, global mentorship and industry exposure
body_text:
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 3:06PM by PIB Mumbai Release ID: 2340310 Views: 87 A A Print Share X Facebook Instagram WhatsApp Copy Article Link
Read in: English Gujarati
Goa, 23 November 2026 The Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT), India’s National Centre of Excellence for Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR), signed an MoU with Wacom India at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 to strengthen India-Japan cooperation in creative technologies and skill development. The partnership aims to expand access to professional tools and industry-led training for Indian students. Under the agreement, 18 students across IICT’s three two-year diploma programmes in Animation Film Design, Interactive Video Game Design & Development, and Post Production & VFX will receive 50% tuition scholarships, along with accommodation assistance for eligible outstation students. The collaboration will also provide structured mentorship and global exposure through 10 Wacom-branded creative contests and quarterly masterclasses on Manga, Anime and other creative disciplines, led by Japanese and Indian artists and experts, by December 2027. The two institutions will jointly develop a global student portfolio showcase covering digital illustration, concept art, character design, animation and game art, enabling students to build industry-ready portfolios. The agreement also provides for IICT’s integration into Wacom tablet packaging and its Pixel Perch creator platform, subject to mutually agreed implementation plans. Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Ashish Kulkarni, Founding Director, IICT, said that connecting young creators with global ecosystems is essential to growing India’s creative economy. He noted that the partnership brings together Japan’s strengths in animation, manga and gaming with India’s diverse storytelling heritage, enabling students to create original intellectual property for global audiences. Dr. Vishwas Deoskar, Chief Executive Officer, IICT, highlighted the importance of practical experience in enhancing employability in the AVGC-XR sector. He said that contests, masterclasses, professional tools and portfolio development would help students work on real-world briefs and demonstrate their industry readiness. Koji Yano, Global Head of the Creative Experience Unit, Wacom, highlighted the potential for creative collaboration and knowledge exchange between India and Japan across animation, manga, gaming and digital content. He said Wacom’s technologies, including digital ink, would enable young Indian creators to collaborate and participate in global creative partnerships. About IICT: The Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT), India’s National Centre of Excellence for Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR), was established in collaboration with the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India, Government of Maharashtra, FICCI and CII. Its first campus began operations at the NFDC Complex in Mumbai, in July 2025, while a permanent campus is being developed at Film City. IICT currently offers 18 courses and has partnered with leading global technology and media companies.
